newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Sivensa expects June loan for new plant.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Sivensa expects June loan for new plant.

text.p: Leading Venezuelan steel company Sivensa expects to get by June some $625 million in loans for a long-planned hot briquetted iron (HBI) plant, company executives said.
"We reckon we'll get the loans ready by June," finance director Neil Malloy told Reuters.
The 2,000 tonnes per year plant, which will use FINMET technology, is a $700 million joint venture with Australian mining company Broken Hill Proprietary.

Production of the briquettes, which can be used to substitute for increasingly rare high quality scrap, should begin at half capacity in January 1999, Malloy said, rising to full capacity by June the same year.
Malloy said the financing would be provided by banks loans backed by government credits from the U.S.'s Eximbank, Germany's Hermes and Australia's OKB.
Broken Hill has a 50 percent stake in the project, which is in south-eastern Venezuela, Sivensa some 30 percent, while state-owned company Orinocco Steel (FMO) holds the remainder.
